farm.name: MADA double-crop paddy lot on marine clay
farm.region: Muda Agricultural Development Authority (MADA) granary, Kedah-Perlis plain
farm.headline: Malaysia's rice bowl: two paddy seasons a year on canal water that runs short when the dry monsoon fails.
farm.story: A 2.4 ha paddy lot inside the MADA scheme, planted twice a year (main season from about August, off-season from about February) with direct-seeded rice. The Muda and Pedu dams supply the water, but El Niño years such as 2016 and 2024 forced MADA to delay or cut the off-season. Continuous paddy carries planthopper, blast and weedy rice, the straw is usually burnt, and yields have plateaued near 4.5-5 t/ha a season.
challenge_tags: Off-season water shortfall in El Niño years
Rice after rice: weedy rice and planthopper

irrigation.label: MADA gravity canal (Muda/Pedu dams)
irrigation.source: Muda and Pedu reservoirs via the MADA canal network

baseline_rotation.name: Paddy - paddy (two seasons a year)
baseline_rotation.note: Sentinel-2 shows two green-up and harvest cycles every year since 2020, matching the MADA two-season calendar.

water_context.in_situ_source: MADA and JPS reservoir storage reports, Muda and Pedu dams
water_context.note: Water comes from surface reservoirs, not groundwater. When Muda and Pedu storage falls below about 40% at the end of the dry monsoon (Jan-Mar), MADA delays the off-season or rotates supply between blocks.

rice.note: BERNAS-licensed mills buy at the government floor price; input and price subsidies apply.

grain_maize.note: Feed mills in Kedah and Penang take local grain corn under the national grain-corn programme, but need a dryer.

sweet_corn.note: Pasar tani and roadside sellers along the Alor Setar corridor.

mung_bean.note: Small market; a buyer or cooperative has to be arranged before planting.

groundnut.note: Local snack processors; most groundnut is imported.

watermelon.note: Middlemen collect for the northern wholesale markets.

precip.method: Inverse-variance weighted mean of MERRA-2 (55 km), GPM IMERG (10 km) and the nearest MetMalaysia rain gauge (GHCN-Daily). Weights come from each product's monthly error against the gauge; the gauge's own weight shrinks with its distance from the field.

ground_provenance.note: The gauge is 106 km from the field. Tropical storms are a few kilometres wide, so daily totals differ a lot between the gauge and the field; monthly and seasonal totals agree far better. Days the station did not report are left out, not counted as dry.

soil_moisture.method: MERRA-2 / SMAP-class relative wetness x Saxton-Rawls saturation for this field's SoilGrids texture.

facts.headline: About 2399 mm of rain a year
facts.detail: Year-to-year swing is 13%. The wettest months are Sep, Oct, Nov. Annual total is rising 162 mm per decade (a clear trend).
facts.dataset: MERRA-2 meteorology + GPM IMERG precipitation (daily, point)

facts.headline: Satellite rain reads 5% higher than the nearest rain gauge
facts.detail: Penang International gauge, 106 km away: 2390 mm; GPM IMERG 2503 mm; MERRA-2 2287 mm a year. The fused estimate leans 10% on the gauge, less the farther away it is.

facts.headline: 46% of the year's soil-moving rain falls in Sep, Oct, Nov
facts.detail: 56 days a year bring more than 12.7 mm. The biggest single day on record was 138 mm. Heaviest-day rainfall is rising 6.7 mm per decade (a clear trend).
facts.dataset: MERRA-2 meteorology + GPM IMERG precipitation (daily, point)

facts.headline: 2 days a year reach 35 C
facts.detail: The last eight years averaged 2 such days against 1 in the first eight. The count is flat over the record. Mean temperature is rising 0.28 C per decade (a clear trend).
facts.dataset: MERRA-2 meteorology + GPM IMERG precipitation (daily, point)

facts.headline: No frost: the monsoons, not temperature, set the planting calendar
facts.detail: The wettest three months are Sep-Nov (891 mm) and the driest Jan-Mar (290 mm). Rain exceeds evaporative demand in 10 months of the year, so a second or third crop depends on where the dry months fall and on irrigation.
facts.dataset: MERRA-2 meteorology + GPM IMERG precipitation (daily, point)

facts.headline: Rain exceeds evaporative demand 2.1 times over the year
facts.detail: Reference evapotranspiration is 1168 mm a year against 2399 mm of rain. In Jan-Mar demand exceeds rain by 72 mm.
facts.dataset: MERRA-2 meteorology + GPM IMERG precipitation (daily, point)

facts.headline: 0.8 notably dry root-zone months a year recently, 3.5 in the early 2000s
facts.detail: A dry month is one where root-zone wetness sits more than one standard deviation below normal for that month. Driest years: 2002, 2005, 2016. Main-season root-zone wetness is rising 0.011 units (0-1 scale) per decade (not statistically clear yet).
facts.dataset: Root-zone soil wetness GWETROOT, standing in for SMAP L4

facts.headline: From orbit the field looks bare or dormant in 4 months of the year
facts.detail: Sentinel-2 (10 m) greenness (NDVI) averages under 0.30 in Mar-May, Oct and peaks at 0.88 in Dec (2020-2024, 85 clear looks).
facts.dataset: Sentinel-2 L2A NDVI (B08/B04), SCL cloud mask

facts.headline: Acrisols (clay loam, SoilGrids 250 m), 7.8% organic matter
facts.detail: The root zone can hold about 202 mm of plant-available water. pH 5.6, drainage: moderately well drained.
facts.dataset: Soil properties 0-100 cm (texture, SOC, bulk density, pH, CEC, water retention)

facts.headline: Hydrologic group C: this soil takes rain in slowly
facts.detail: Erodibility (Kw) is 0.121, on a scale where 0.2 is resistant and 0.5 is very erodible. Tolerable loss is taken as 11 t/ha a year (a default; SoilGrids does not map soil depth to rock).
facts.dataset: Soil properties 0-100 cm (texture, SOC, bulk density, pH, CEC, water retention)

facts.headline: Slope about 1.6% at 5 m elevation
facts.detail: From SRTM 30 m elevation over a 180 m window (4 m of relief).
facts.dataset: SRTM GL1 30 m elevation (3x3 window, Horn slope)

facts.headline: Sentinel-2 sees about 1.8 crop cycles a year
facts.detail: Green peaks per year, 2020: 1, 2021: 2, 2022: 2, 2023: 3, 2024: 0. Crops usually peak in Jul, Nov. The satellite counts cycles; it does not name the crop.
facts.dataset: Crop cycles counted from Sentinel-2 NDVI peaks

facts.headline: FAO GAEZ rates this area's crop suitability
facts.detail: Highest rated here: Hill rice (dryland padi bukit) (high, 76/100), Cassava (ubi kayu) (good, 62/100), Paddy rice (irrigated) (good, 61/100). Projected to lose most by the 2050s (RCP8.5): Sweet potato (-12 points).
facts.dataset: Crop suitability index, high inputs (1981-2010 and 2041-2070 RCP8.5)
